title: Erdős-Hajnal Conjecture (Conjecture 3)
statement_text: Every graph $H$ satisfies the Erdős-Hajnal property, i.e., there exists a constant $\delta > 0$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices contains either a clique or an independent set of size $n^\delta$.
context_text: The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture asserts that forbidding a fixed graph $H$ as an induced subgraph forces large homogeneous sets, in sharp contrast with random graphs where the maximum clique/independent set is only $O(\log n)$. The conjecture has been verified for all graphs on at most four vertices, the bull, cliques, and graphs constructible from them by substitution.
paper_contribution: Proves that a constructive version of the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture implies the improved approximation conjecture (Conjecture 5), and shows the improved approximation property is closed under graph substitution, establishing Conjecture 5 for many graphs $H$ (e.g., $P_6$-free, fork-free) where the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture remains open.
paper_title: An algorithmic weakening of the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture

title: Conjecture 5 (Improved Approximation Conjecture)
statement_text: Every graph $H$ satisfies the improved approximation property, i.e., there exists a constant $\varepsilon > 0$ such that MIS admits a (randomized) $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-approximation polynomial algorithm on every $H$-free $n$-vertex graph $G$.
context_text: MIS (Maximum Independent Set) asks for a largest independent set; an $r$-approximation algorithm outputs an independent set of size at least $\mathrm{OPT}/r$. A graph $G$ is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. In general $n$-vertex graphs MIS is NP-hard to approximate within $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. $H$ satisfies the Erdős–Hajnal property if there is $\delta>0$ such that every $H$-free $n$-vertex graph has a clique or an independent set of size $n^\delta$, and the constructive Erdős–Hajnal property if moreover such a set can be found in polynomial time. The conjecture is an algorithmic analogue of the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture: the inapproximability of MIS in general graphs could always be beaten in any class defined by one forbidden induced subgraph. The two are not known to be comparable. On one hand, MIS is polynomial-time solvable in $P_6$-free and fork-free graphs, so these graphs satisfy the improved approximation property while it is open whether $P_5$ has the Erdős–Hajnal property. On the other hand, the authors prove that every $H$ with the constructive Erdős–Hajnal property with constant $0<\delta\le 1/2$ satisfies the improved approximation property with any constant below $\delta-\delta^2$ (all graphs known to have the Erdős–Hajnal property have the constructive version). They also prove that the improved approximation property is preserved under substitution (replacing a vertex of $H_1$ by a copy of $H_2$), the operation known to preserve the Erdős–Hajnal property.
paper_title: An algorithmic weakening of the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture

title: Question: optimal approximation exponent for MIS in H-free graphs
statement_text: For a given $H$, what is the largest $\varepsilon > 0$ such that MIS admits an $O(n^{1-\varepsilon})$-approximation algorithm in $H$-free graphs?
context_text: MIS (Maximum Independent Set) asks for a largest independent set; an $r$-approximation algorithm outputs an independent set of size at least $\mathrm{OPT}/r$. A graph $G$ is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. In general $n$-vertex graphs MIS is NP-hard to approximate within $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. $H$ satisfies the Erdős–Hajnal property if there is $\delta>0$ such that every $H$-free $n$-vertex graph has a clique or an independent set of size $n^\delta$, and the constructive Erdős–Hajnal property if moreover such a set can be found in polynomial time. $H$ satisfies the improved approximation property if for some $\varepsilon>0$ MIS has a (randomized) polynomial-time $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-approximation on $H$-free graphs; the authors conjecture every $H$ has it and here ask for the best exponent. Partial results of the paper: a graph $H$ is locally easy if it has a universal vertex $v$ such that MIS is polynomial on $(H-v)$-free graphs (e.g. $H-v$ is $P_6$, the fork, or $tK_{1,3}$), and for locally easy $H$ MIS can be $\sqrt{\mathrm{OPT}}$-approximated on $H$-free graphs (in particular $\sqrt n$ for triangle-free graphs); MIS can be $\mathrm{OPT}^{1-1/t}$-approximated on $K_{t+1}$-free graphs, and local search gives $O(\mathrm{OPT}^{1-1/t})$ on $K_{t,t}$-free graphs. On the negative side, in triangle-free graphs the ratio cannot be improved to $n^{1/4-\varepsilon}$ unless $\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{BPP}$ (it is NP-hard to distinguish $\alpha(G)\le n^{5/6-\varepsilon}$ from $\alpha(G)\ge n^{1-\varepsilon}$), with generalizations to graphs of girth $\gamma+1$.
notes: Posed as an open research direction in running prose in the 'Results and organization' section; partially investigated within the paper but not fully resolved.
paper_title: An algorithmic weakening of the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture
